resources.title: Pitch cover with brand mark
resources.purpose: Open an investor pitch with the company name, the customer outcome in one line and the round being raised.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Open an investor deck with who the company is, what it does in one plain sentence, and what it is asking for.
Modify: Edit `deck`: company name (it is set as type, not drawn), the one-sentence description, round, amount, date and contact. Keep the sentence to three lines at this width and the name short enough to stay left of column 7 (about eight letters at 208 px).
Invariant: The name is the first read, the sentence the second, the round and date the third. No illustration, no tagline, no logo mark; the amount matches the ask page.
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: Replace the wordmark and edit the mark() function (leaf path + tally strokes) or swap in your own SVG logo.
Rewrite the headline as the outcome a customer gets, keeping one italic emphasis word.
Update the round, date and confidentiality line in the footer rule.
Recolor the hero field through the --tp-* tokens in pack.css if your brand palette differs.

resources.title: Problem as an illustrated scenario
resources.purpose: Make the customer pain concrete by following one purchase through a week, then size the loss in three numbers.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Size the customer problem with evidence the investor can check, and make it concrete with one real kitchen.
Modify: Replace `kitchens` with your own audit (one value per customer or interviewee) and `example` with one of them; the headline fraction, median line, callout and description recompute.
Invariant: Bars start at zero and are sorted; the median is computed, not typed; exactly one bar is highlighted and it is the one the callout describes; the source line says how the data was collected.
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: Pick one real customer and one real item; write five dated moments from decision to loss.
Edit the stations array (icon, time, headline, quote line); add an icon to the icons map if needed.
Set purchases and binnedShare (or your own loss inputs) so the stat band and headline agree.
Keep exactly one highlighted station: the moment the cost becomes visible.

resources.title: Market sizing (TAM/SAM/SOM)
resources.purpose: Size the market bottom-up with nested circles whose areas are computed from the values, each value showing its own multiplication.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Size the market bottom-up so an investor can redo the arithmetic: who is counted, how many, at what price.
Modify: Edit `price` and the three `tiers` (kitchen counts and the one-clause definition of who is counted); SOM is a share of SAM by a stated year. Values, bars and the headline recompute.
Invariant: Value = locations × price for every row; bars share one linear scale starting at zero (the SOM bar is meant to look small); SOM is labelled as a plan, not a forecast; the price matches the unit-economics page.
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: Define one unit (location, seat, household) and its annual contract value.
Count units for TAM, SAM and SOM from sources you can cite, and state the SAM filter in one clause.
Edit the tiers array; circle radii use √(value/TAM) so areas stay honest.
Rewrite the method box with your price basis and what you deliberately excluded.

resources.title: Business model & unit economics
resources.purpose: Show how one customer makes money and how fast it repays its acquisition cost, with a churn-adjusted payback curve.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Show how one customer makes money and how long it takes to repay what it cost to win.
Modify: Edit `unit` (price, cost lines, CAC, churn, onboarding ramp). The P&L column, the curve, the payback marker, the 24-month multiple and the headline recompute. Use the churn you report on the traction page.
Invariant: The curve is cumulative and churn-adjusted; the CAC line and the curve share one axis that starts at zero; the payback month is computed, not typed; the P&L lines add up.
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: Enter price per unit per month and the itemised cost to serve.
Enter blended CAC and monthly churn from your last full cohort.
Check the payback month and LTV/CAC that the page computes; rewrite the headline to match.
Rename the source line to the cohort and period the inputs come from.

resources.title: Traction chart with milestones
resources.purpose: Prove momentum with one honest monthly growth series and dated milestones that explain the inflections.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Prove momentum with one honest monthly series and two numbers that say the product works and customers stay.
Modify: Replace `months` (live customers at month end; ARR = live × price), `cancelled` and the before/after audit values. Every label, the headline and both metrics recompute.
Invariant: Bars start at zero with no axis break; only the latest month is in the accent; ARR uses the same price as the market and unit-economics pages; churn is cancellations over billed customer-months.
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: Replace months and the monthly driver series (customers, locations or revenue).
Add two or three milestones by month index; use row to stagger labels that would touch.
Replace the three rail metrics with retention, outcome and churn figures you can defend.
Let the headline quote the multiple the page computes rather than a rounded boast.

resources.title: Team and the ask (use of funds)
resources.purpose: Close the pitch with who will execute, how much is being raised, where it goes and what it buys.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Close the pitch with the amount, where it goes, what it buys and who will do it.
Modify: Edit `ask` (raise, runway, fund shares, CAC, price, today’s numbers) and `founders` (one credential each, the one that matters for this company). Dollar amounts, the kitchen target and target ARR recompute; the module throws if the shares do not sum to 100%.
Invariant: One proportional bar for use of funds, labelled in place; new kitchens = sales budget ÷ CAC (churn not netted, as the source line says); target ARR = target kitchens × the same price as the other pages; the accent marks the money that buys the milestone.
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: Replace the team array with four people and one proof line each; monograms regenerate from names.
Set the raise and use-of-funds shares (they must sum to 1).
Set the target units, ACV and date the round is meant to reach.
Keep the advisors line to named roles, or remove it if you have none.

resources.title: 四半期レビュー表紙（四半期ダイヤル付き）
resources.purpose: 対象四半期を年度内の位置で示し、結論となる3指標を最初の1枚で伝える。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 会議の名前・対象期間・日付・作成者だけを静かに示し、資料の素性を一目で分かるようにする。
Modify: doc の会社名・年度・四半期・会議日・作成部署を書き換える。対象期間（4月始まりの年度）と曜日は自動計算。3月決算以外の会社は firstMonth の式を自社の期首月に合わせる。
Invariant: 文字だけで構成する（ロゴ・図・数値サマリーを置かない）。結論は2ページ目以降で述べる。社外秘などの取扱区分は実際の規程に合わせる。
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: fy と q を対象の年度・四半期に変える（ダイヤルと月表示が追従）。
summary の3指標を、本文ページと同じ値・同じ定義で入れ替える。
各指標の増減の向き（dir）と良否（good）を別々に設定する。
会議名・日付・作成部署を差し替える。

resources.title: KPIタイル（スパークライン付き）
resources.purpose: 主要KPI 6つの今期値・計画比・前年比・8四半期推移を並べ、未達の指標を一目で示す。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 主要指標の実績を計画・前年同期と並べ、どれが計画に届かなかったかを1つの表で示す。カードを並べず、上から順に読める表にする。
Modify: kpis に指標を足し引きする（6〜8行まで）。各行は8四半期の実績（今期が最後）、今期計画、kind（金額＝増減率％、比率＝差pt）、better（低いほど良い指標は down）を持つ。計画比・前年同期比・未達の判定・見出し・推移線は自動。quarters と source、running も更新する。
Invariant: 赤は未達の行の計画比だけに使い、必ず「未達」と書く。▲や▼は使わない（日本の帳票では▲はマイナスを表す）。前年同期比は4四半期前との比較。推移線は形を見るためのもので、縦軸は行ごとに異なると注記する。
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: kpis 配列に8四半期の実績、今期計画、単位、小数桁を入れる。
解約率など下がるのが良い指標は better:'down' にする。
比率の指標は kind:'pt'、金額や件数は kind:'ratio' を選ぶ。
見出しは未達指標と主因を1文で書き、サブ行で原因ページに誘導する。

resources.title: 前年差の要因ウォーターフォール
resources.purpose: 前年同期から当期への利益の変化を、増減要因ごとに分解して示す。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 営業利益が計画に対してなぜ上振れたかを要因別に分解し、上振れの「質」を問う。数字の大きさではなく、どの要因が効いたかを見せる。
Modify: plan・actual・drivers（計画との差、符号付き、百万円）を書き換える。合計が合わなければエラーになる。focus を付けた要因が紺で強調され、右欄の「その要因を除いた計画差」と見出しが自動で再計算される。hiring と右欄の説明文は自社の事情に合わせる。
Invariant: 計画（枠線）＋要因＝実績（塗り）。棒はゼロから立ち上げる。強調する要因は1つだけ。増減の向きは色ではなく位置と符号で示す。
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: start に前年同期の値、steps に符号付きの要因を入れる（合計は自動計算）。
軸の上限 yMax と目盛を実データの範囲に合わせる。
右側の注記は影響の大きい3要因に絞り、各要因の具体的な中身を書く。
見出しの差額と利益率は自動計算の値をそのまま使う。

resources.title: ファネルとボトルネック
resources.purpose: 獲得ファネルの件数と段階間の転換率を前期と比べ、最も悪化した段階とその影響額を示す。
resources.notes:
Purpose: リードから受注までの各段階を前期と比べ、どの段階で取りこぼしたかを1か所に絞って示す。右欄で「その段階が前期並みならどうだったか」を金額にする。
Modify: stages（段階名・転換率の呼び名・今期と前期の件数）と newArr（今期実績と計画、2ページと同じ値）を書き換える。最も悪化した段階、その強調、右欄の受注件数と新規ARRの試算、見出しの数値は自動。cause と右欄の要因の文は実際の調査結果に合わせる。
Invariant: 棒の長さは件数に比例し、全段階で同じ目盛り（受注の棒が短いのは実際に少ないから）。強調は1段階だけ。試算は「その段階だけ前期の転換率、他は今期の転換率、平均受注額は今期」という前提を右欄に書く。
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: stages に各段階の今期・前期の件数を入れる。
newArr（または受注金額）を入れると平均受注額と影響額が計算される。
ボトルネックは前期差が最も悪い段階として自動選択される。意図と違う場合は根拠を確認する。
右パネルの仮定（下流の転換率は今期値）を変えた場合は注記も直す。

resources.title: コホート・ヒートマップ
resources.purpose: 契約月コホートごとの継続率を経過月で並べ、施策前後のコホートを同じ経過月で比べる。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 契約時期ごとの継続率を経過期間で揃えて並べ、施策の前と後のコホートを同じ経過期間で比べる。
Modify: cohorts（契約時期と、経過1四半期目からの継続率）を実データに置き換える。changeFrom は施策後の最初のコホート、compareAt は比べる経過四半期。色の段階、比較列の枠、平均、見出しの差は自動。コホートは8つ程度まで（それ以上は半期単位にまとめる）。
Invariant: 色は1色相の明度だけで、数値も全セルに書く（16px以上）。比較は同じ経過期間どうしで行い、まだ到達していないコホートは平均に含めない。
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: grid を実データ（行＝契約月、列＝経過月、未観測は null）に置き換える。
changeAt に施策後の最初のコホートの行番号を入れる。
比較する経過月（例ではM3）を決め、枠と右側の平均値を合わせる。
色の範囲 lo/hi を実データの最小・最大に合わせ、凡例を確認する。

resources.title: 次四半期の重点施策と決裁事項
resources.purpose: 分析から導いた次四半期の施策を、根拠・KPI・責任者・日程つきで示し、会議で決める事項を1つ明記する。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 本資料の分析から導いた次四半期の重点施策を、責任者・KPI・期限つきで合意する。会議の最後に「誰が・何を・いつまでに」を確定させるページ。
Modify: priorities を3件（多くても4件）に絞って書き換える。各施策に根拠のページ、KPI（現状→目標）、責任者1名、期限1つを置く。KPIの現状値は funnel・onboarding・cloud の今期の値から計算される。quarter、note、running も更新する。
Invariant: 上から重要な順に並べる（1が最優先）。施策は動詞で終わる具体的な行動にする。責任者は部署名ではなく個人名と役職。期限は日付で書く。
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: items に施策を4〜5件入れ、それぞれ根拠ページとKPI（現状→目標）を1つずつ書く。
span・ms・plan を月単位（0＝期初、3＝期末）で設定する。
責任者は部署と個人名を1名に絞る。
決裁事項は1件にし、金額と期待効果を本文ページの数値と一致させる。

resources.title: 戦略提案の表紙
resources.purpose: 提案の宛先・問い・到達目標を示し、選択と集中を表す正方形のモチーフで提案全体の性格を伝える。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 誰に、何の提案を、いつ・どの場で出すのかを一目で伝える。結論は次のページから。
Modify: deck の提出先・題名・到達目標（年度と利益率）・日付・会社名・担当者・機密区分を差し替える。題名は2行以内に収める。
Invariant: 表紙に図や飾りを置かない。到達目標の数字は推奨案のページ（2029年度 6.0%）と一致させる。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: 宛先・題名・提案者・日付を差し替える。
副題を「何を・いつまでに・どこからどこへ」の1文にし、from・to・year を実際の目標にする。
右の正方形は cols・rows・chosen・rec で、検討数・評価数・推奨の関係に合わせる。
色を変える場合は pack.css の --s-green と --s-ochre を変える。

resources.title: 論点ツリー
resources.purpose: 主論点をサブ論点と検証可能な問いに分解し、各問いの仮説・効果・検証状況を一覧にする。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 「6%に届くか」という大きな問いを、検証できる問いと数値の仮説に分け、どこに改善余地が集まっているかを示す。
Modify: plan（売上・利益・前提）と tree（論点・問い・仮説・効果）を差し替える。合計、必要額、棒の長さ、接続線は自動で計算される。focus: true の論点が強調色になる。
Invariant: 線は分解を表し、順序ではない。各問いは「はい／いいえ」で答えられる形にし、仮説には必ず数値を入れる。効果の単位と年度は全ページでそろえる（2029年度・億円）。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: 主論点を「〜するには何をすべきか」の1文で書く。
branches にサブ論点を2〜4個、各サブ論点に Yes/No で答えられる問いを2〜3個入れる。
各問いに仮説・効果（同じ単位）・状態（done/wip/todo）を入れる。
下の示唆は、検証済みの効果の合計と残る論点から1文で書く。

resources.title: 2×2優先度マトリクス
resources.purpose: 打ち手を効果と実行の容易さの2軸に置き、明記した閾値で最優先の組み合わせを選ぶ。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 論点ツリーで洗い出した打ち手を「効果」と「実行の容易さ」で並べ、どれから着手し、どれを見送るかを決める。
Modify: levers の効果（億円）・容易さ（1〜5）・ラベルの側 side を差し替える。境界 cut を変えると色分け、網掛け、右の表の合計が追従する。ラベルが境界線や図の端にかかる場合は自動で反対側に置かれる。
Invariant: 打ち手の番号と効果は論点ツリーと同じ値にする。境界は明記した数値で引き、目分量で決めない。容易さの採点方法を注記する。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: moves に打ち手ごとの容易さ（1〜5）、効果（金額）、投資額を入れる。
閾値 easeCut・impactCut を事前に決めた基準で設定する。
重なるラベルは lab（t/r/l）で位置を変える。
右の一覧と見出しの件数は自動で追従するので、脚注に採点方法を書く。

resources.title: 選択肢比較表（ハーベイボール）
resources.purpose: 実現手段の選択肢を同じ評価軸で並べ、推奨案の強みと弱みを定性・定量の両面で示す。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 実現手段の3案を同じ評価軸で並べ、推奨案がどこで優れ、どこで劣るかを隠さずに見せる。
Modify: effect（打ち手別の効果）、options（含む打ち手・投資・回収の計算方法）、judged（4段階の評価と根拠）を差し替える。営業利益・利益率・回収年数は自動で計算される。rec: true の列が網掛けになる。
Invariant: 評価軸はすべて「●ほど良い」の向きにそろえる。数値で言えるものは数値で書き、評価記号には必ず短い根拠を添える。推奨案の弱点も残す。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: options に2〜4案と一行説明を入れ、推奨案に rec:true を付ける。
criteria はすべて「●ほど良い」向きの表現にし、各セルに0〜4点と一言の根拠を書く。
quant に利益率・投資額・回収期間など同じ定義の数値を入れる。
見出しは推奨案の弱点も含めて書く（例：利益改善では劣るが…）。

resources.title: 推奨案とその根拠
resources.purpose: 推奨案を一つに言い切り、目標に届く利益率ブリッジと、選ぶ理由3つを並べる。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 推奨案を1つに絞って言い切り、営業利益が2025年度の実績から2029年度の計画までどう積み上がるかを示す。
Modify: option（推奨案）、sales（売上高）、steps（増減要因と金額、kind）、conditions（実現の条件と期限）を差し替える。最後の合計、利益率、見出しの数値は自動で計算される。
Invariant: 合計＝前の合計＋増減の和（入力で上書きしない）。外部要因（売上の伸び・コスト上昇）は灰色、打ち手は強調色に分け、マイナスの要因も必ず載せる。条件の日付はロードマップと一致させる。
Static: 静的ページ。
tags: エグゼクティブサマリー
deriveSteps: base と levers（寄与pt・開始時期）を入れると到達値が計算される。
target に目標値を入れ、到達値との差を確認する。
理由3つは比較表の評価軸と対応させ、それぞれに数字か条件を1つ入れる。
左パネルの2指標は本文の数値と同じものを使う。

resources.title: 実行ロードマップ（ガント）
resources.purpose: 推奨案の実行順序・期間・判断の時期を四半期単位で示し、会議で決める事項で締める。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 推奨案をいつ・どの順で実行し、各年度末にどの指標がどこまで動くかを1枚で約束する。
Modify: axis（期間）、phases（段階）、work（打ち手ごとの期間と節目、月番号は2026年4月＝0）、kpis（年度末の値）を差し替える。営業利益率は営業利益と売上高から計算される。
Invariant: 打ち手の番号は論点ツリーと同じにする。節目の日付は推奨案ページの「実現の条件」と一致させ、2029年度末の値は推奨案の数値（利益率6.0%）と一致させる。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: years に対象期間の四半期を並べ、phases で大きな段階を区切る。
streams に論点ツリーの番号と対応するワークストリームを入れ、a・b を四半期番号で指定する。
gates に日付と「何を決めるか」を入れる。
最下段の枠には、この会議で決めてほしい事項を1つだけ書く。

resources.title: 学会発表の表紙（主張タイトル＋研究対象の図版）
resources.purpose: 何を達成した研究かをタイトルの一文で示し、発表者・所属・会議情報と研究対象の模式図を一枚にまとめる。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 発表の題目と、誰が・どこで・いつ話すのかを一目で伝える表紙。タイトルだけで研究の対象と条件（ラベル50枚・ひび割れ検出）がわかるようにする。
Modify: talk の title（2行に分けた配列）・subtitle・authors・affiliations・venue・date・session を書き換える。発表者に presenter:true を付けると名前の前に○が付く。曜日は date から自動で求める。
Invariant: タイトルは2行以内で、句の途中で改行しない。著者の上付き数字と所属の番号を一致させる。会議名・日付・セッションは表紙にだけ置き、各ページには繰り返さない。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: talk の会議名・日付・セッション番号を実際の予定に置き換える
タイトルを『何を・どの条件で達成したか』の一文にし、副題に手法名を書く
著者と所属番号を対応させ、発表者に presenter:true を付ける
右の図版を研究対象の模式図か実画像に替え、図説に縮尺・出典を書く

resources.title: 背景と問い（概念図つき）
resources.purpose: 研究の動機となる制約を比例した概念図で示し、検証する問いを条件つきの一文で置く。
resources.notes:
Purpose: なぜラベルが足りないのかを、作業の単位（1画素）と作業時間の掛け算で示し、研究の問いを置く。
Modify: cost の枚数・橋の数・1枚あたりの時間・正解を付けた枚数を実際の値にする（右の計算と時間は自動で再計算）。crack の座標と幅を変えると (a)(b) とその説明文の画素数・割合が再計算される。実画像を使う場合は (a) を画像に替え、(b) は実際の正解マスクにする。
Invariant: (a) と (b) は同じ範囲・同じ縮尺。模式図であることを図の下に書く。右の計算は 枚数 × 時間 = 合計 の順で、単位を省かない。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: data の件数・コストを自分の研究の実数に置き換える（格子は自動で比例する）
左の3項目を『現状・制約・困りごと』の順に一文ずつ書く
(b) の図を研究対象の典型的な失敗例に描き替える
問いに比較対象・条件・評価指標を含めて一文で書く

resources.title: 手法パイプライン図（3段階）
resources.purpose: 手法を処理順に並べ、各段階の入力・目的・出力と段階間で受け渡すものを明示する。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 手法の全体（教師が擬似ラベルを作り、生徒が学ぶ）と、新しい一点（2段のしきい値）を1枚で示す。上段は流れ、下段は同じ確率マップでの比較。
Modify: setup の枚数としきい値を書き換える。下段の確率マップは crack から合成した模式図で、途切れの数と残る画素の割合は自動で数える。実データの例に替える場合は prob を実際の確率マップに置き換える。
Invariant: 提案部分（2段のしきい値と擬似ラベル）だけを青にする。学習の流れは左から右、更新の戻りは下から上。下段の3枚は同じ範囲・同じ縮尺。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: stages の段階名・入力データ・3行の仕様を自分の手法に書き換える
handoffs に段階間で実際に受け渡すもの（重み・中間データ）を書く
各段階の小図を、その段階の入力と出力が分かる絵に描き替える
損失や指標の定義を図の下の脚注に一文で書く

resources.title: 結果（95%信頼区間つき折れ線図）
resources.purpose: 主結果を信頼区間つきで示し、主条件の値と比較対象との差、誤差棒の定義を同じページで読めるようにする。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 主結果を区間付きで示し、「ラベル50枚の提案法 ≈ 教師あり学習の200枚」という読み方を図の上で確かめられるようにする。
Modify: labels・methods（各枚数の平均とSD）・runs・full を自分の結果にする。区間（t分布）、見出しの比較相手と比率、右端の値、注記はすべて同じ配列から再計算される。横軸の枚数は2倍刻みにそろえると等間隔の目盛が対数目盛と一致する。
Invariant: 提案法だけを青、比較手法は灰色の濃淡と線種で区別する。区間の定義（何回の試行・何の区間・計算法）を図のすぐ下に書く。縦軸は0から始めない代わりに目盛の数値を必ず出す。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: series に各条件の平均と標準偏差（試行ごと）を入れ、runs と tCrit を試行回数に合わせる
full（上限の参照値）と focusN（主条件）を設定する
右の定義欄に区間の種類・試行回数・計算式を実際の手順どおりに書く
タイトルを主条件での差を述べる一文にする

resources.title: アブレーション表（区間図つき）
resources.purpose: 構成要素を外した結果とハイパーパラメータの感度を、差と信頼区間を並べた一枚の表で比べる。
resources.notes:
Purpose: どの構成要素が効いているのかを、提案法との差と区間で読ませる表。差の大きさを1本の目盛にそろえて比べる。
Modify: full と groups の各行（IoU の平均、差のSD、途切れ）を書き換える。差・区間・点の位置・見出しの数値（最大の要素と倍率）は自動で再計算される。行を増やすと表の高さも伸びるので、6〜7行までにとどめる。
Invariant: 差は同じ試行どうしの対応のある差で、区間の定義を表の下に書く。目盛はすべての行で共通、0（提案法）に基準線。区間が0をまたぐ行は白抜きの点にする。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: ref に提案法の値、groups に外した構成・変えた設定の行を入れる
列見出しの指標名と単位、差の向きを自分の指標に合わせる
区間図の目盛 S.min / S.max を全行の区間が収まる範囲にする
表の下に全行共通の条件と指標の定義を書く

resources.title: 結論と限界・今後の課題
resources.purpose: 数値つきの結論、同じ重みの限界、今後の課題を並べ、主要な比較を一本の目盛で再掲して締める。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 発表の締め。主張とその適用範囲を見出しの一文で言い切り、貢献・限界・今後を短い箇条で残す。
Modify: facts の数値を結果・アブレーションのページと同じ値にする（ここだけ別の数を書かない）。lists の各項目は1〜2行に収め、2項目ずつにとどめる。contact を発表者に替える。
Invariant: 貢献には条件（ラベル枚数・比較相手）と数値を添える。限界は貢献と同じ大きさの文字で書き、注記に押し込まない。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: r と recap の数値を結果ページと同じ値にそろえる
結論を条件つきの数値で2項目以内に書く
限界に『検証していない範囲』と『ラベルや指標の不確かさ』を書く
最後の一文を聴衆に持ち帰ってほしい考え方にする

resources.title: Postmortem cover with impact summary
resources.purpose: Open an incident review with what happened, when and what it cost users, backed by one representative slow trace.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Open the review with what happened and what it cost customers, in units, before anyone argues about causes.
Modify: Edit incident, impact and summary. The duration, failure share and every impact line are computed from them; keep the summary to one paragraph of four sentences: trigger, mechanism, effect, end.
Invariant: Times in one zone (UTC), stated once. Every number has a unit and a window. Name systems and changes, never people.
Static: Static page; no builds.
deriveSteps: Set the incident id, severity, date window and triggering change in inc
Replace the four KPIs with your measured impact, each with unit and window
Paste one real slow trace (span start/end in ms) into trace; the waterfall rescales
Rewrite the title as the user-visible symptom plus its trigger

resources.title: Layered system architecture (zones, sync/async edges, incident path)
resources.purpose: Show where each component lives, how requests and events move between them, and which path failed.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Show where the failing path runs through the system and which shared component turned a cache problem into a checkout problem, so the review discusses the design, not the symptom.
Modify: Edit zones (width, sub-column widths), parts (zone, col, row, name, role) and links. Box positions, ports and orthogonal routes are computed; the figure refuses zone widths that do not add up. Keep roles to one fact each, under 25 characters.
Invariant: Line style = call type (solid synchronous, dashed asynchronous, dotted replication); red = incident path and degraded components only; arrows point from caller to callee; zone labels stay clear of every edge; nine components or fewer.
Static: Static page; no builds.
deriveSteps: List your zones (top to bottom) and set node boxes per zone in N
Declare each edge as sync, async or repl and route it orthogonally between node ports
Mark the failing path with hot:true on edges and nodes
Add at most two annotations stating the measured symptom on the hot path

resources.title: Request sequence diagram with alt frame
resources.purpose: Show the order of calls for one request and exactly where the failing branch adds time.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Show, on a true time axis, how much of the gateway's budget the fallback query consumed, so the fix is placed on the hop that spends the time.
Modify: Replace trace, lanes, spans and messages with one representative trace (times in ms from the first request). Bar lengths, arrows, the remaining-time bracket and the headline numbers are computed; keep the axis domain a little past the timeout.
Invariant: Time runs left to right on one linear scale and is never broken; the timeout line spans every lane; red marks only the degraded components; say it is one request, and state how a healthy request compares.
Static: Static page; no builds.
deriveSteps: Set lanes to the services on the request path, left to right in call order
Write msgs in time order as call/return pairs; add hit/miss frames with frequencies
Put measured durations on the slow messages and the timeout on the final return
Anchor a note to the message that introduced the defect

resources.title: Latency percentiles over time (p50/p95/p99, SLO, events)
resources.purpose: Show how far and for how long latency exceeded its objective, with the deploy and rollback events that explain the shape.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Show how far and how long checkout latency left its objective, with the three changes that shaped the curve.
Modify: Replace `data` with your 1-minute percentiles (t, p50, p95, p99) and edit SLO, TIMEOUT and events. The impact window, minute counts, headline and description are computed from the data.
Invariant: Percentiles are computed per bucket from raw requests, never averaged across buckets; requests cut off by the timeout count at the timeout, which caps p99 — say so. Linear time and latency axes from zero. Red only for the customer-impact window.
Static: Static page; no builds.
deriveSteps: Replace the generator with exported per-bucket percentiles (t, p50, p95, p99)
Set SLO, bucket size and the change events (deploy, alert, rollback)
Check that the side panel and title read true from the derived values
State the population and how timeouts are counted in the method note

resources.title: Incident timeline (system vs response lanes, TTD/TTM/TTR)
resources.purpose: Reconstruct what the system and the responders did on one time axis and derive detection, mitigation and recovery times from it.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Reconstruct the incident minute by minute and show where the response lost time, with detection, mitigation and resolution times computed from the same timestamps.
Modify: Edit events (t, text, optional mark), axisBreak, domain and lessons. The vertical positions, label spreading, impact bar, brackets, durations and the headline numbers are computed; marks impact, detected, mitigated and resolved must exist.
Invariant: One time zone, stated once. Time is to scale inside each axis segment and any break is drawn and labelled. Durations are measured from the start of customer impact and never typed by hand. Lessons describe systems and gaps, not people.
Static: Static page; no builds.
deriveSteps: Enter events with UTC times, lane (system or response) and 1–2 short lines
Mark impact, alert, cause, mitigate and recovered events so durations compute
Keep one time zone for the whole page
Replace the lesson cell with the one thing that most delayed recovery

resources.title: Risk matrix with owned mitigations
resources.purpose: Close the review with the risks exposed, the planned effect of each action, and who owns it by when.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Close the review with the actions it commits to, each tied to the specific failure mode it removes, so nobody leaves with a list of good intentions.
Modify: Edit actions (action, owner, due, removes, status, doneOn) and the review date. The headline counts and the last due date are computed. Keep one owning team per action and one failure mode per row; write failure modes in the words used on the earlier pages.
Invariant: Every row has an owner, a date and the failure mode it removes; status is a word, not a colour; rows follow the order in which the failure unfolded, then detection and mitigation.
Static: Static page; no builds.
deriveSteps: List each risk with current and planned [likelihood, impact] on 1–5 scales
Give every mitigation one owning team, a due date and a status
Adjust band thresholds only if your organisation defines them differently
Check that the headline still matches the computed band counts

resources.title: Evaluation report cover with dataset card (splits, class balance)
resources.purpose: Name the model, the decision requested and the data it was tested on, with split sizes, class balance and label provenance, before any metric appears.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Before any metric, show what the model was tested on: later data than it was trained on, separated by guard weeks, with the same rare failure rate in every split.
Modify: Edit report, splits (first and last Monday, pump-weeks, failures, use) and guards; keep TEST identical to the shared block on pages 02–06. Bar positions, week counts, rates and the headline are computed, and the module refuses a test split that disagrees with TEST.
Invariant: Splits follow calendar time with test last; the time axis is linear; failure rates are shown for every split; the guard rule is stated in words.
Static: Static page; no builds.
deriveSteps: Enter your splits with period, unit counts and per-class counts
Rewrite the class definitions exactly as the labels were produced
Fill the facts with unit/window, label source and known gaps
State the decision the report asks for in the spec list

resources.title: Confusion matrix (row-normalised, counts shown)
resources.purpose: Show where each true class ends up and which confusions dominate, with per-class precision and recall beside it.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Show what the chosen threshold does in counts — failures caught, failures missed, false alarms — and make the expensive error impossible to overlook.
Modify: Replace the shared block (identical on pages 02–06) with your scored test set; edit cost and the alternative threshold. Every count, rate, cost and the headline are computed from rows.
Invariant: Rows are the truth, columns the model’s decision; counts and rates appear together; the missed-failure cell is the emphasised one; the threshold and the alert volume it implies are stated.
Static: Static page; no builds.
deriveSteps: Replace the shared rows block with real test predictions (true class, predicted class, scores)
Keep the class order and state the normalisation in the caption
Check that the headline counts come from the computed matrix
Write the decision rule that produced the predicted class

resources.title: ROC and precision–recall curves with thresholds
resources.purpose: Show ranking quality and the alert trade-off for a rare positive class side by side, with the same thresholds marked on both.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Compare the model with what maintenance does today at equal effort, because crews, not thresholds, are the scarce resource.
Modify: Replace the shared block (identical on pages 02–06); edit scorers if your baseline differs. Curves, average precision, both operating points, the equal-effort line and the table are computed from rows.
Invariant: Precision–recall, not ROC, because failures are 1% of pump-weeks; the no-skill line is drawn; both operating points use the thresholds actually in use; model in blue, baseline in grey.
Static: Static page; no builds.
deriveSteps: Replace the shared rows block with real scores and labels for the positive class
Set MARKS to the thresholds under discussion and THRESHOLD to the proposed one
Keep the chance diagonal and the prevalence baseline
Translate the operating point into alerts per week for the audience

resources.title: Feature importance with uncertainty intervals
resources.purpose: Show which inputs the model relies on, with the spread across repeats, so small or null effects are not over-read.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Show which inputs the model actually relies on, with their uncertainty, so a reviewer can check that the signal is physical (current, vibration, heat) and not an artefact (station, age).
Modify: Replace inputs with your permutation results (mean and percentile interval per input, plain-language labels, a short name for the headline) and REPEATS; keep the shared block identical to pages 02, 03, 05 and 06. Order, highlighting, hollow markers, the base AP and the headline are computed.
Invariant: Name the metric, the split, the number of repeats and the interval; keep the zero line; inputs whose interval includes zero are hollow and grey, never ranked as if they mattered.
Static: Static page; no builds.
deriveSteps: Compute permutation importance on the test split with repeats; enter mean and percentile interval per feature
Name the metric that was degraded and the baseline value
Note correlated features that share credit
Keep the zero line and the hollow style for intervals that include zero

resources.title: Calibration plot (reliability diagram, ECE, Brier)
resources.purpose: Show whether predicted probabilities can be read as risks, before and after calibration, with bin counts and intervals.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Show whether predicted probabilities can be read as risks, because thresholds and alert budgets are set on them.
Modify: The shared test-set block is repeated on pages 02, 03, 05 and 06 (modules cannot import each other); replace it identically on all four. Replace the shared rows block with real predictions (raw and calibrated scores); bins, observed shares, Wilson intervals, ECE, Brier score and the histogram are computed.
Invariant: Equal-width bins, stated. The diagonal is the reference. Show how many windows fall in each bin (most are near zero for a rare class) and put an interval on each observed share. Fit the calibrator on validation, never on the test split.
Static: Static page.
deriveSteps: Replace the shared rows block with raw and calibrated scores for the test split
Keep equal-width bins and show the count per bin
Say where the calibrator was fitted (never on the test split)
Point the table at the bins around your operating threshold

resources.title: Model card: intended use, limitations, subgroup results
resources.purpose: Close the report with what the model is for and not for, what is known to be weak, subgroup performance with intervals, and the decision requested.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Close the report with what the model is for, what it must not be used for, what is known to be weak, and the decision requested with its safeguards.
Modify: The shared test-set block is repeated on pages 02, 03, 05 and 06 (modules cannot import each other); replace it identically on all four. Rewrite the three lists for your model. Replace the shared rows block and the site assignment with real subgroup labels; recall and Wilson intervals are computed. Keep the decision box to one request plus its conditions.
Invariant: Limitations carry the same visual weight as intended use. Subgroup results show n and an interval, and the weakest subgroup is named in the limitations. Out-of-scope uses are stated plainly.
Static: Static page.
deriveSteps: Rewrite intended use and out-of-scope uses in plain operational terms
Replace the site assignment with real subgroup labels; keep n and intervals
Name the weakest subgroup in the limitations
State the decision with the conditions that would pause it

resources.title: 講義の表紙と学習目標（Lecture cover + learning goals）
resources.purpose: 講義の題名・対象・所要時間を示し、受講後にできるようになる3つの行動を最初に約束する。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 講義の題名と、終わったときに何ができるようになるかを最初に約束する。受講者が自分の到達を確かめられる目標にする。
Modify: course の講座名・回・題名・副題・対象・時間と goals を書き換える。目標は「〜できる」で終わる観察できる行動にし、3つまでにする。
Invariant: 目標の順番は講義の順番と同じ。まとめのページでは目標を繰り返さず、学んだ要点として言い直す。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: course の講座名・回数・題名・対象・所要時間を実際の講義に合わせる
goals を「説明できる／計算できる／見抜ける」のような観察できる行動で3つ以内に書き直す
天秤イラストの pans を講義の中心例（2つの量と重み）に置き換えるか、主題に合う手描き図に描き替える
最終ページのまとめと目標が1対1で対応しているかを確かめる

resources.title: 概念図：てんびんで見る加重平均（Concept illustration）
resources.purpose: 抽象的な概念（加重平均）を、数直線上でつり合うてんびんという1枚の具体的な絵で理解させる。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 加重平均を「客数を重りにしたときのつり合いの点」として一枚の図で理解させる。式の前に、位置と重さの直観を作る。
Modify: stores（客単価と客数）と unit を書き換えると、積む個数・つり合いの点・確かめの式がすべて再計算される。客数は unit の倍数にする。範囲 domain は全店の客単価が入るように広げる。
Invariant: 横軸は等間隔の目盛の数直線。重りは1個＝100人の同じ大きさの四角で、店の客単価の位置に積む。つり合いの点だけを藍色にし、計算した値の位置に置く。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: 説明したい概念を、身近な物理的な比喩（重さ・流れ・容器など）に1つ対応させる
stores の値を講義の例に置き換え、支点と比較点が数直線上の正しい位置に来ることを確かめる
凡例の3行で「位置・重り・支点」が何を表すかを具体的な言葉で書き直す
確認メモの計算（距離×人数）が左右で一致することを読み上げて検算する

resources.title: 例題のステップ解説（Worked example, step by step）
resources.purpose: 問題・データ表・途中式を1段ずつ示し、受講者が手元で同じ計算を追いかけられるようにする。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 加重平均の計算手順を、受講者が電卓で追える速さで一段ずつ見せる。手順の文と、その手順が作る数字を同じ高さに置く。
Modify: stores（店名・客単価・客数）を書き換えると、売上・合計・答えが再計算される。steps の文は「何をするか」を動詞で書く。
Invariant: 数字は右そろえで桁をそろえ、演算子は独立した列に置く。途中の式を省かない。答えは単位つきで、藍色はこの答えだけ。
Static: クリックごとに 手順1（各店の売上）→ 手順2（合計）→ 手順3（割り算と答え）が現れる。最終状態ではすべての式と答えが読める。
deriveSteps: 問題文と表を実際の例題に置き換え、表の列と式で使う量を一致させる
steps の見出しを「〜を出す／〜を合計する／〜で割る」のような動詞で書き、式は data から生成する
答えのカードに単位と「なぜそうなるか」の1文を添える
段階表示の順序を声に出して確かめ、最終状態で全式が読めるかを確認する

resources.title: よくある誤りと正しい考え方（Common mistake vs correct reasoning）
resources.purpose: 典型的な誤りと正しい考え方を同じ縮尺の図で並べ、考え違いの原因とズレの大きさを示す。
resources.notes:
Purpose: よくある誤り（店ごとの平均をそのまま平均する）と正しい計算を、同じ目盛の上で並べ、ずれの大きさと原因を一目で示す。
Modify: stores と unit を書き換えると、上下の重り・つり合いの点・差の円と割合が再計算される。上の数直線は「1店＝1つ」、下は「100人＝1つ」のまま使う。
Invariant: 上下の数直線は同じ範囲・同じ目盛。誤りの値だけ朱、正しい値だけ藍。誤りを責めず、「何を同じ重さとして数えたか」の違いとして説明する。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: 受講者が実際によくする誤りを1つ選び、誤りの式と正しい式を同じ例で書く
両方の図を同じ縮尺・同じ部品で描き、違いが1か所だけになるようにする
説明文は原因を1文で述べ、相手を責める言い方を避ける
下段のズレ（差と割合）を計算で出し、実務でどう見分けるかを1文添える

resources.title: 理解度チェック（Quiz with answer note）
resources.purpose: 同じ考え方を別の場面で使えるかを選択問題で確かめ、クリック後に計算つきの解答を示す。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 学んだ考え方（合計 ÷ 合計）を、客単価ではなく購入率という別の場面で使えるか、その場で確かめる。
Modify: stores の来店客と購入率を書き換えると、正解と3つの誤答（平均の平均・重みの取り違え・大きい店だけ）が計算し直され、小さい順にア〜エが振られる。値が重なる場合は来店客か率を変える。
Invariant: 誤答はすべて実際に起きる誤りから計算する。解答では各選択肢の誤りに名前を付ける。正解だけ藍、平均の平均だけ朱。
Static: 1回目のクリックで正解の囲みと各選択肢の理由、つり合いの図と式が現れる。最終状態（PDF）では解答まで読める。答えを隠した配布にしたい場合は、このページを解答の前後2枚に分ける。
deriveSteps: 例題とは別の場面で、同じ考え方を使う問題を1つ作る
選択肢に正答1つと、典型的な誤り（例：単純平均）から出る値を含める
アイコンと帯の数値を teams から生成し、問題文の数値と一致させる
配布用に答えを隠す場合は、解答注記を次ページへ移す

resources.title: まとめと次回予告（Summary + next session）
resources.purpose: 講義の要点を3つの行動に言い換えて持ち帰らせ、次回の内容につなげる。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 講義の要点を3つと式1つに絞り、明日の仕事で使う確かめ方として持ち帰らせる。次回につなぐ。
Modify: formula・cases・points・next を書き換える。cases にはこの回で実際に計算した例だけを入れる。要点は1行に収まる長さにする。
Invariant: 要点は3つまで、1枚目の目標の順（説明する→計算する→確かめる）に対応させるが、同じ文は繰り返さない。式は分数の形で、言葉で書く。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: 1枚目の学習目標と対応する要点を3つ、結論の1文で書く
本文には理由か、明日から使える具体的な行動を書く
アイコンを要点の中身を表す手描き図に描き替える
次回予告を実際の講座計画に合わせる（なければ質問の受付方法などに置き換える）

resources.title: Typographic essay opener
resources.purpose: Open a visual essay with one display-size title, a one-sentence dek and a single drawn image cropped by the page edge.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Open a long-form piece the way a literary magazine does: one title the reader remembers, one sentence that says what the piece is about, and who wrote it.
Modify: Edit `story`. Keep the title to one line (about 20 characters at 128 px; shorten it rather than shrinking the type) and the dek to one or two sentences.
Invariant: Title first, dek second, byline third. The title is set in one color and one style, no italic or coloured word; no image on this page; no folio on an opener.
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: Write a two- or three-word title and a one-sentence dek that states what the essay is about
Replace the masthead name, issue and byline with your publication's own
Redraw the cropped illustration (or place a high-resolution photograph) that shows the essay's subject
Check the title at full size: it should wrap only where the design breaks it

resources.title: Image-led spread with essay column
resources.purpose: Let one photograph carry the page while a single column of essay text explains why it matters.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Begin the essay text beside one photograph, so the reader meets the subject and the voice together.
Modify: Replace `photo` (keep a raster within 1.3× of its native width: this one is shown at 1.05×) and `essay` (about 100–130 words; the first paragraph takes the drop cap).
Invariant: The caption says what the picture shows and carries the credit; the photograph is not cropped beyond its own frame; the drop cap spans exactly three lines and is the only rust mark on the page.
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: Choose a photograph with enough pixels for a 650 px wide crop and write a caption that says what it shows
Credit the photograph and its licence on the page
Rewrite the headline and a 60–80 word column around one idea
Check the drop cap and the last line of the column for awkward breaks

resources.title: Pull quote
resources.purpose: Stop the reader on one sentence that carries the argument, with a short lead-in column beside it.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Give the reader a pause and the essay’s argument in one sentence, at a size that cannot be skimmed.
Modify: Replace `quote.text` with a sentence from your own text (about 15–25 words, so it sets in three or four lines). Quote a person only with their real, sourced words and name them.
Invariant: One sentence; the opening quotation mark hangs outside the text edge; the rust quotation marks are the only colour; this is the only dark page in the pack.
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: Pick one sentence from your own text (or a real, sourced statement) that carries the argument
Attribute it truthfully: to the section it comes from, or to the real speaker with a source
Highlight at most one word
Replace the side column with the paragraph that leads into the quote

resources.title: Illustrated timeline on a log time scale
resources.purpose: Show the order of a process and how long each stage takes when durations differ by orders of magnitude.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Make a contrast of scale felt: 7 months of waiting against a 28-second pour, without a log scale that hides it.
Modify: Edit `journey` (days per stage, in order) and `lastMinute` (seconds, one item marked pour). Stage widths, inside/outside labels, the magnification factor, the headline ratio and the closing note recompute.
Invariant: Both rows are linear and the same width; row 2 is exactly the last minute of row 1; only the pour is rust; durations are labelled on the marks; the source says the values are typical, not measured.
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: List the stages in process order with a duration in seconds and a human label
Redraw each small illustration so it shows its stage
Keep the log scale named in the lede and on the axis; switch to a linear scale if all durations are similar
Replace the source line with where the durations come from

resources.title: Big-number spread
resources.purpose: Give a few numbers headline scale across a two-page spread, each with its unit and caption, plus the figures derived from them.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Show that the 28 seconds are one setting among five, and give each number a sentence that says what it controls.
Modify: Edit `recipe` (dose, yield, time, temperature); the ratio and the flow rate in the time row recompute. Rewrite the headline in the way a practitioner says the recipe aloud, and update `words` if the numbers change.
Invariant: Every numeral carries its unit; derived numbers are computed, not typed; the numerals share one size and line up on their right edge; no colour on this page.
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: Choose two to three numbers that belong together and write what each one counts
Compute any ratio or rate from those numbers in the module, not by hand
Keep units next to every number and the bars on one shared zero
Replace the source line with the actual source of the numbers

resources.title: Closing page with next-issue teaser
resources.purpose: End the essay on one line the reader can carry away, point to what comes next and credit every image used.
resources.notes:
Purpose: End the essay on its own last paragraph, then tell the reader who wrote it and where every picture and number came from.
Modify: Replace `ending` with the real final paragraph (two to four sentences; any durations must agree with the timeline page), `author` with a one-line note, and `credits` with one entry per image, chart or data source in the piece.
Invariant: The end mark closes the text and is the only colour; no summary of takeaways and no slogan; every image used in the piece is credited here with its licence.
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: Write one closing line that returns to the essay's opening idea
Replace the teaser with what the reader can read or do next
List credits and licences for every photograph and illustration in the piece
Redraw the illustration so it echoes the opener

resources.title: 表紙と成果の大きな数字（Cover + headline KPIs）
resources.purpose: 表紙で1年間のいちばん大きな変化を1文で示し、成果を4つの大きな数字と前年度比で一覧させる。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 表紙を兼ねて、どの団体の何年度の報告かと、この一年の変化を平易な一文と4つの数字で伝える。
Modify: org、districts（地域別ページと同じ表）、prev（前年度）、sessions、stay、exam を差し替える。文中の増分と4つの数字は計算で出る。
Invariant: 数字は4つまで。どの数字にも「何を数えたか」を添える。率は分母を書く。一文は事実を言い、標語にしない。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: 表紙の見出しを、1年間でいちばん伝えたい変化の1文に書き換える
kpis を4つまでに絞り、それぞれ単位・何を数えたか・前年度値を入れる
率の差は「ポイント」、量の差は「%」で表示されることを確認する
町並みのイラストを団体の活動に合う風景に描き替える

resources.title: 地域別の活動：抽象タイル図と順位表（Regional activity, tile schema）
resources.purpose: 地域ごとの参加者数・拠点数を、地理を捏造しない抽象タイル図と順位表で示し、次の拠点計画の根拠を示す。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 地区ごとに「支援が必要な子どものうち、どれだけに届いているか」を比べ、次の教室をどこに開くかの根拠を示す。
Modify: districts の教室数・参加者数・対象者数を差し替える。割合、並び順、市全体の値、強調する地区（割合が最も低い地区）は自動で決まる。note には強調した地区の事情を一文で書く。
Invariant: 割合の分母（対象の子ども）を必ず表に出す。参加者の合計は1ページ目の486人と一致させる。地図は使わない（位置関係を捏造しない）。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: regions に地域名・人数・拠点数を入れ、タイルの col/row でおおまかな位置関係を決める
見出しの割合と「最も混み合う地域」が計算どおりかを確認する
合計行が表紙の数字と一致することを確かめる
正確な地図がない限り、ページ上の「模式図」の注記を残す

resources.title: 事業の流れ：ロジックモデル（Inputs → activities → outputs → outcomes）
resources.purpose: 投じた資源から子どもに起きた変化までを4段階で並べ、成果の数字がどこから来たかを1枚で説明する。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 1年間の事業を「使った資源→行ったこと→直接の結果→子どもに起きた変化」の順に並べ、成果の数字がどこから来たか、どう測ったかを1枚で示す。
Modify: K（各ページと共通の数値）と stages の項目・測り方を差し替える。各段階は3項目まで。
Invariant: 事業費は予算ページ、参加者数は1・2ページと同じ値にする。アウトカムには必ず測り方（調査名・時期・人数）を添える。線は想定する流れであり、変化がすべて事業の効果だとは言わない。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: K に年間の主要数値を入れ、他のページと同じ値になっているか確認する
各段に2〜3項目、数字と「何を数えたか」を書く
アウトカムの割合には調査方法・時期・回答数を注記する
めざす姿（インパクト）を団体のミッションの1文に書き換える

resources.title: 予算の内訳：支出ドーナツと収入の積み上げ（Budget breakdown）
resources.purpose: お金の出入りを1枚で示し、支出のうち現場に使った割合と、収入−支出＝繰越の関係を計算で一致させて見せる。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 寄付と委託費がどこに使われたかを1本の帯で示し、子ども一人・1回あたりの費用に言い換えて実感できる大きさにする。
Modify: spend（万円、room: true が教室の運営費）と income、参加者数・延べ参加数を差し替える。帯の幅、割合、ラベルの段、一人あたりの費用、見出しの「約◯万円」は自動で計算される。
Invariant: 帯の合計＝支出合計。一人あたり＝支出合計÷実人数、1回あたり＝支出合計÷延べ参加。割り算の式をページに残す。事務局の費用も隠さない。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: spend と income に決算の数値（同じ単位）を入れる
見出しに使う「現場」の項目に field: true を付ける
中央の合計・下段の収支式が決算書の合計と一致することを確かめる
割合の四捨五入で合計が100%にならない場合、注記が出ることを確認する

resources.title: 受益者の声（架空と明記した例示）（Beneficiary voices）
resources.purpose: 数字では伝わらない変化を、子ども・保護者・支える側の3つの立場の声で補う（例示は架空と明記）。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 数字では伝わらない変化を、本人・家庭・学校という3つの立場の言葉で確かめる。
Modify: voices を、本人の了解を得た実際の声に差し替える（最初の声が大きく入る）。立場と所属は、個人が特定されない粒度にとどめる。source に集め方を書く。
Invariant: 声は短く、言い換えずに載せる（要約した場合は注記する）。架空の声を実在の声として見せない。顔写真やイラストを添えない。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: 本人の同意を得た実際の声を3つ選ぶ（立場が重ならないように）
属性は学年・拠点・活動年数など、個人が特定されない粒度にする
各カードのタグに、その声が示す変化を短く書く
実際の声に差し替えたら「架空」の表示と注記を外す

resources.title: 次年度計画：数値目標とロードマップ（Next-year plan）
resources.purpose: 今年度の結果から次年度の重点を導き、現状→目標の数値と四半期ごとの実行計画を1枚で示す。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 今年度の結果から次年度の重点を導き、数値目標と四半期ごとの実行計画を1枚で約束する。
Modify: goals の目標値と方法、plan の期間（四半期の番号 0〜3）とマイルストーンを差し替える。現状値は表紙・地域別ページと同じ regions から計算する。
Invariant: 目標は現状値と並べ、増分（%・ポイント・か所）を計算で示す。計画は約束ではなく予定として書き、確定していない項目は断定しない。
Static: 静的ページ。
deriveSteps: goals に現状値（今年度の実績）と目標値を入れ、増分の表示を確認する
plan の各行に四半期の期間とマイルストーンを入れる
見出しは今年度の結果から導いた重点を1文で書く
確定していない日程は「予定」と注記する

resources.title: Launch hero with product mockup
resources.purpose: Open a product or feature launch with one promise, the availability facts and a believable picture of the product in use.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Open a launch with the product's name, what changed in one sentence, when customers get it, and one real piece of the product so the claim is concrete.
Modify: Edit launch.name, launch.changed (one sentence, a mechanism, not a slogan), launch.availability (dates and plans) and the rule fragment (one object from your product, worded as the UI shows it).
Invariant: The name appears once in the deck, here, in green. The fragment is flat, legible (18 px) and labelled as sample data; no device frame. Dates must match the close.
Static: No builds.
deriveSteps: Rewrite the headline as the one job the release does for the customer, in two lines.
Replace the three facts with your real launch date, plans or regions.
Edit the queue, KPI and reason arrays so the mockup shows your own product's main screen.
Keep the sample-data note unless the screens show real, cleared data.

resources.title: Feature grid with bespoke icons
resources.purpose: Show what is new as six concrete jobs, each with a custom icon and the plans that include it.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Say what is new as jobs the product now does, each backed by one number from real use, so the audience can map features to their own work.
Modify: Edit features (3–4 items): plans (must match 04-pricing), name (fits one line at 26 px in columns 1–3), does (one sentence, two lines at most), proof (one measured number) and what (what it measures, ≤ 36 characters). Edit beta for the evidence base.
Invariant: One number per capability, each with its unit and what it measures; the evidence base is stated in the source line. Plans agree with the pricing page.
Static: No builds.
deriveSteps: List the new capabilities as jobs the product now does, one verb-led sentence each.
Pick or draw an icon per job using the shared grammar (tile, line weight, one accent).
Set the plan tag for each feature and check it against your pricing page.
Cut to three features if the rest are minor; the grid keeps its rhythm.

resources.title: Before/after workflow on a shared time axis
resources.purpose: Prove a launch benefit by showing which workflow steps disappear and where the time goes, on one honest hour axis.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Prove the launch's main claim with one concrete case: where a return's time went before, and what is left of it now.
Modify: Edit the two phase lists (minutes from the request; kind team/customer/carrier/auto; after:true for steps that no longer hold up the refund) and the lane names. Bars, durations, both refund ticks, the headline and the description recompute. Raise DAYS if the slower lane is longer than four days.
Invariant: Both lanes share one axis that starts at the request. Unchanged time (the carrier) stays visible in both lanes so the gain is not overstated. Green is 2.0 only; dark grey is time spent waiting on your team.
Static: No builds.
deriveSteps: Time one real case end to end and split each step into waiting, staff work, customer and automated parts.
Enter both workflows in the arrays; set maxH to cover the longer one.
Keep steps that do not change so the comparison stays honest.
Rewrite the headline to state the measured change in plain words.

resources.title: Pricing tiers with unit cost
resources.purpose: Let each buyer find their plan by volume, see what an upgrade adds and compare the effective cost per unit.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Let each buyer find their plan by monthly volume, see what the upgrade adds, and know which plan we recommend and why.
Modify: Edit plans (price, included returns, overage, features, limits, support) and the rows list; mark one plan with pick:true. The headline, the green rule and the title follow the data. Keep feature names identical to 02-features.
Invariant: One row per attribute, identical across plans, so absence shows as a dash. Exactly one recommended plan, marked only by its middle position and the rule over its column. Currency, tax and billing terms in the note.
Static: No builds.
deriveSteps: Enter each plan's price, included volume and overage rate.
Mark feature availability per plan in the has arrays, in the same order as the feature names.
Choose at most one highlighted plan and give the badge a factual reason.
State currency, tax and billing terms in the source line.

resources.title: Integration map with one event chain
resources.purpose: Show where a product sits among existing systems and which single event produces the customer-visible benefit.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Show where the product sits among systems the customer already runs — which system connects at which step — and what this release adds.
Modify: Edit steps (in order), systems (rows) and links (system, step, what passes in ≤ 15 characters, isNew for this release). Positions, drops, colours, the key and the description follow the data.
Invariant: One row per system, one column per step, in the order a return happens. Green only for what is new in this release, and the key names it; everything else is grey.
Static: No builds.
deriveSteps: List the systems that send data in and the systems your product acts on.
Label each edge with the data it carries, pointing the way data moves.
Pick the one event chain that creates the benefit and number its steps.
Rewrite the headline to name that chain's outcome.

resources.title: Launch closing: next steps and rollout
resources.purpose: End a launch with the concrete adoption steps, the rollout dates per plan and where to go next.
resources.notes:
Purpose: End a launch with the dates that matter, the first three things a customer does, and what happens to what they have now.
Modify: Edit dates (mark the launch day today:true; must match the hero), start (three imperative steps, in order), migration (what moves by itself, what the customer must do, by when) and contact.
Invariant: Dates in order on one rule; only today's dot is green. Steps are numbered because they are a sequence. Future items are stated as dates, not promises.
Static: No builds.
deriveSteps: Write three imperative steps a customer can take this week, in order.
List rollout dates by plan or region; mark anything uncertain as planned.
Replace the URL with your announcement or docs page.
Keep the headline to one short instruction.

resources.title: 全体ステータス（RAG表示＋一言要約）
resources.purpose: 定例の冒頭で、全体の状態・その理由・判断が必要な領域を1枚で伝える。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 会議の冒頭1枚で、全体の状況・その理由・今日決めてほしいことを伝える。細部は2ページ以降に任せる。
Modify: overall と areas の状況（ok／warn／late）、dev・bufferWeeks・uat の数値、asks（判断事項と期限）を書き換える。完了見込み日・遅れの週数・予備期間の残りは自動計算。project の会議名と日付、asOf（基準日）は全ページで同じ値にする。
Invariant: 状況は色の点と言葉（順調／注意／遅延）を必ず併記する。全体の判定は最も悪い領域を無視しない。要点は3つまで、1行目が結論、2行目が根拠。判断事項には期限を付け、詳細ページを示す。
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: 全体の判定（良好・注意・要対応）と前回の判定を overall に入れる。
領域ごとに状態・前回比・今週の状況を1文で書く。
見出しに「会議で何を決めてほしいか」を書く。
KPIの実績と計画を同じ基準日でそろえ、出典行の日付を合わせる。

resources.title: マイルストーンのタイムライン（今日の位置）
resources.purpose: 基準計画に対してどこがどれだけずれ、最終期限に影響するかを1本の日付軸で示す。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 基準計画に対してどの工程がどれだけずれ、予備期間と本番稼働日にどう響くかを1本の日付軸で示す。
Modify: phases の plan（基準計画）と fc（実績・見込み）、state、進行中の工程の status、buffer、cutover、asOf を書き換える（YYYY-MM-DD）。ずれの週数、予備期間の残り、見出しは自動。期間が変わったら span も直す。
Invariant: 基準計画の線は消さずに残す。見込みは基準日時点の実績から計算した日付にする（3ページのバーンダウンと同じ日付）。状況の色は言葉と一緒にだけ使う。本番稼働日を最後の行で必ず示す。
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: フェーズごとに基準計画と見込み（実績）の開始日・終了日を入れる。
予備日がある場合は buffer に期間を入れる。
today を報告基準日にする。
見出しを「遅れの大きさと吸収方法」を述べる文に書き換える。

resources.title: バーンダウン（計画線・実績線・完了見込み）
resources.purpose: 残作業の推移を計画と比べ、現在のペースでいつ終わるかを数字で示す。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 開発の残作業を計画線と比べ、今のペースだといつ終わるかを日付で示す。遅れを「感覚」ではなく速度から説明する。
Modify: sprint（初日・日数・計画スプリント数）、scope、done（各スプリントの完了ポイント）、added（変更要求で増えたポイント）、change の注記を書き換える。残り・平均速度・完了見込み日・必要なペース・見出しは自動。見込みに使うスプリント数は lookback で変える。
Invariant: 縦軸は0から。計画線は当初計画のまま残し、スコープの追加は注記で示す。見込みの計算方法（直近3スプリントの平均）を注記に書く。完了見込み日は2ページの工程表と一致させる。
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: 週次の残作業（ポイントまたは件数）を remaining に入れる。
計画の総量と完了週を initialScope と planWeeks に入れる。
途中で増えた作業は scopeChanges に記録する。
見込みに使う週数 lookback を決め、出典行に計測条件を書く。

resources.title: RACI表（責任分担）
resources.purpose: 作業ごとに実行者と最終責任者を合意し、特定の役割への負荷の偏りを見つける。
resources.notes:
Purpose: 次の工程の主な作業について、誰が実行し誰が最終責任を持つかを合意し、今日決めるべき体制の穴を示す。
Modify: roles（列）と tasks（行と各役割の R／A／C／I）を書き換える。各行の A がちょうど1つでないと読み込み時にエラーになる。focus を付けたセルが強調され、見出しの役割名に使われる。ask の人数・期限・内訳を実際の依頼に合わせる。
Invariant: 文字だけで表す（色付きの札にしない）。A は各行1名、A と R の兼務は A/R と書く。役割は個人名でなく役割名で書く。強調するのは今日の判断に関わるセルだけ。
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: 列に役割、行に主要な作業を並べる（10行程度まで）。
各行に A をちょうど1名置き、R・C・I を埋める。
R の件数の偏りを確認し、注記と見出しに反映する。
本番移行など重要な行に key: true を付ける。

resources.title: リスク・課題一覧（影響×確度）
resources.purpose: リスクと課題を同じ尺度で並べ、今週どれに手を打つかを担当と期限つきで決める。
resources.notes:
Purpose: リスクを同じ物差しで並べ、上位のリスクに誰がいつまでに何をするかを確認する。今日の判断で手当てできるものを区別する。
Modify: risks の各行に、発生可能性 l と影響度 i（1〜3）、上位に入るものには内容・対応策・責任者・期限、判断事項で手当てするものには decision（6ページの番号）を書く。並び順・表に載る上位3件・図の位置・見出しの件数は自動。
Invariant: 優先度はグレーの濃さで示す（状況の色は使わない）。表のリスクには必ず責任者と日付の期限を付ける。今日の判断に関わるリスクだけをアクセント色にする。評価日と評価者を注記に書く。
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: リスクと課題を ID・内容・影響・確度で items に入れる（6件前後）。
各項目に対策・担当・期限を1行で書く。
スコアの閾値（15以上・8以上）が自社基準と合うか確認する。
見出しに最優先の項目と期限を書く。

resources.title: 決定事項と次のアクション
resources.purpose: 定例の最後に、決まったこと・誰がいつまでに何をするか・次回の議題を確認する。
resources.notes:
Purpose: ステアリングコミッティに判断してほしいことを、選択肢・推奨案・期限つきで示し、その場で決められるようにする。
Modify: decisions を書き換える（2件まで。3件以上は2ページに分ける）。各判断に title・due（期限）・比べる列（columns）・options・reason を置く。開発スコープの案は cut（削るポイント）と extraVelocity（増える速度）から完了日を計算するので、dev は3ページと同じ値にする。
Invariant: 各判断に推奨案は1つ。推奨の行は太字と「推奨」の文字で示し、色だけに頼らない。期限は日付で書く。選択肢には「何もしない」案も含め、その結果を書く。
Static: Already static.
deriveSteps: 会議で決まったことを決定番号・決定者・理由つきで書く。
アクションを担当1名・期限日つきで actions に入れる。
today を会議日にし、期限超過が正しく表示されるか確認する。
次回の日時・場所・議題を入れる。

resources.title: Cinematic typographic opener
resources.purpose: Open a keynote with the whole argument as one large claim over a generative backdrop that pictures it.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Open a talk with its subject in the room's largest type, the premise in one plain sentence, and who is speaking where — nothing else competes.
Modify: Edit talk.title (two lines at 88 px; about 16 characters per line), talk.premise (two short sentences, one per line: a fact and the size of the answer, not a slogan), talk.speaker and talk.event.
Invariant: Flat paper, ink only — the yellow is reserved for solar data later in the deck. Title hangs from the 64 px top line with the premise under it at y 286 (the upper part of the screen stays visible over the audience's heads); speaker and event share one baseline at 656, the event starting at the centre line (module 12).
Static: No builds; the page reads at once.
deriveSteps: Write the talk's thesis as a two-line claim; put the key word in the accent colour.
Replace the eyebrow with your slot, event and date.
Write one italic subline that says what the talk is about in plain words.
Change SEED until the ridges leave the title area clear.

resources.title: Chapter divider with contour field
resources.purpose: Mark a turn in a keynote and state, in one line, what the coming chapter will prove.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Mark a turn in a long talk and say in one sentence what the next chapter will prove.
Modify: Edit chapters (short claims, not topic labels), set current to this chapter's index, and rewrite sentence with the chapter's key number. Duplicate the file for each chapter and change current only.
Invariant: The number is the same size as the title and sits in grey in modules 0–1; title and sentence hang from row 2 (y 212) at module 2. No yellow on this page — the accent belongs to solar data.
Static: No builds.
deriveSteps: List your chapter titles in the chapters array as short claims.
Set current to this chapter's index.
Write a one-sentence italic lede that previews the chapter's argument.
Reuse the same file for each chapter by changing current only.

resources.title: One giant number with context
resources.purpose: Make one number unforgettable and show, on a small chart below it, exactly where it comes from.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Make one number stick — the hours between peak solar output and peak demand — and show on the same page where it comes from.
Modify: Replace day.demand and day.solar with your hourly profile (25 points, 00:00 to 24:00, GW) and day.date. The number, both peak times, the bracket, the values and the description recompute. Keep the same 2026 day as on 04-then-now.
Invariant: The hero number equals the bracket on the chart and starts at the module of the earlier peak. Both series share one GW axis; yellow is solar only.
Static: No builds; number and chart arrive together.
deriveSteps: Pick the one number the audience should remember and the data it is computed from.
Replace the two profile functions with your data; keep the computed peaks.
Rewrite the serif context sentence so number + sentence read as one thought.
State scaling and data source in the caption under the chart.

resources.title: Then vs now contrast
resources.purpose: Compress a talk's turning point into two parallel, opposing statements, each backed by a small schematic.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Show how the job of every other power source changed in twenty years, on two panels the room can compare without reading numbers.
Modify: Replace each day's demand and solar arrays (25 hourly points, GW) and dates. The yellow wedge, the thick line, the midday low, the evening high, the ramp brackets, the headline numbers and the description recompute. Change MIDDAY/EVENING if your peaks fall elsewhere.
Invariant: Both panels share the 0–15 GW scale, 24 hours and the same marks; yellow is solar only; the thick line is demand minus solar. Keep the later year on the right.
Static: No builds. The 8× difference is visible at once.
deriveSteps: Write the old and new state as two sentences with the same grammar.
Choose years or labels for each half.
Replace the schematics with ones that show the mechanism of each state.
Label both as schematic unless they plot measured data.

resources.title: Quote over a particle field
resources.purpose: Give the audience one sentence to repeat after the talk, set large over a quiet generative field.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Let someone outside the speaker's organisation say, in plain words, that moving load in time already works.
Modify: Replace quote.text (verbatim, at most about 90 characters, real minus signs and units), quote.name (name, role, organisation) and quote.context (why this person knows).
Invariant: Only words someone actually said or wrote, attributed to them. The opening mark hangs so the words align on module 2; the attribution aligns with the words. No yellow — the accent belongs to solar data.
Static: No builds.
deriveSteps: Use a sentence that was actually said or written and note its real source.
Put the first clause in quote.lead so the accent colour lands on the key idea.
Keep it under about 20 words so it holds two lines.
Change SEED if particles crowd the text.

resources.title: Keynote closing with three asks
resources.purpose: Close on the thesis and leave the audience three concrete actions, bookending the opener's imagery.
resources.notes:
Purpose: End on what specific people in the room can do next, and how to reach the speaker; this page stays up during questions.
Modify: Edit close.statement, the asks (who can act; one change each, with a number or a date) and the contact and data lines.
Invariant: Each ask names who acts and what changes, measurably. Three or four asks at most. Contact sits on the opener's bottom line (baseline 656), the data link starting on module 13. No yellow.
Static: No builds; all asks are visible during questions.
deriveSteps: Shorten the opener's thesis into a three-word headline.
Write three asks that start with a verb and name who can act.
Replace the event name and link in the footer.
Check that the asks still read with the builds removed.

resources.title: Horizontal bars: magnitudes on a common zero
resources.purpose: Compare magnitudes across many named categories on one zero baseline, sorted, with the single bar the page is about in the accent and a labelled reference line.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Compare magnitudes against one shared zero baseline, sorted so rank reads at a glance, with the one bar the page is about named in the accent.
Modify: Replace `buildings` (label, value, area). The sort, the highlighted maximum, the median line, the headline ratio and both rail shares recompute.
Invariant: Bars start at zero and use one unit; values are printed at the bar ends; the reference line is labelled with what it is; only one bar carries the accent.
Static: Already static. For a build, pass build:{motion:"grow-x", stagger:60} to the chart.
deriveSteps: Replace `buildings` with your categories in one unit (label, value, plus any second measure such as area).
Keep the descending sort; the accent follows the maximum automatically, or point `worst` at the item your headline names.
Swap the median for your own reference (target, average) and keep its label in the empty space beside the shortest bar.
Rewrite the rail as two shares computed from the same array, e.g. share of the total against share of the size.

resources.title: Grouped bars: two series within repeated categories
resources.purpose: Compare two series inside each repeated category on one zero-based scale, printing the within-pair change so small differences are read rather than guessed.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Compare two series within each repeated category on one shared scale, and make the within-pair change the thing that is read.
Modify: Replace `cohorts` and `years`. The change labels, the count of rises and the largest gain recompute; highlight the series the page is about (here the newer cohort).
Invariant: Both series share one zero-based axis; the pair order never changes between categories; the change is printed, so small differences are not left to the eye.
Static: Already static. For a build, pass build:{by:"series"} to reveal 2024 first, then 2025.
deriveSteps: Replace `cohorts` with your two series names and `years` with categories holding one value per series.
Highlight the series the headline is about; the other becomes context grey and the legend recolours.
Keep the aligned change row: it recomputes series 2 minus series 1 and colours falls with the negative role.
With more than three series or about eight categories, switch to small multiples or a dot plot instead.

resources.title: Stacked bars: composition and total together
resources.purpose: Show what each total is made of and how large each total is, with the component the page is about placed on the shared baseline so it can be compared.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Show what each total is made of and how big the total is, in one bar per category.
Modify: Replace `destinations` and `districts`. Put the component the page is about first so it sits on the common baseline; bars sort by total and the headline recomputes.
Invariant: Segments sum exactly to the printed total; the series order and colors are the same in every bar; only the first segment shares a baseline, so only it (and the total) can be compared precisely.
Static: Already static. For a build, pass build:{by:"series"} to add one destination at a time.
deriveSteps: Replace `destinations` (series) and `districts` (one value per series) in one unit.
Order the series so the component your headline discusses is first and sits on the baseline.
Keep totals printed at the bar ends; the bars sort by total and the headline recomputes.
If shares matter more than totals, pass normalize:true and rewrite the headline in percentages.

resources.title: Diverging bars: signed deviations from a reference
resources.purpose: Show how far each unit sits above or below one stated reference, so direction and size of the deviation read at once.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Compare signed deviations from one stated reference, so above and below read as direction, not just length.
Modify: Replace `depts` (score and headcount). The weighted average, every bar, the headline gap and the rail shares recompute; change the weighting if your reference is a simple mean or a target.
Invariant: Bars start at the reference line, the reference value is printed, signs are written on every value, and positive and negative keep their own colors.
Static: Already static. For a build, reveal the below-average departments last.
deriveSteps: Replace `depts` with your units, scores and group sizes; the weighted reference recomputes (use a plain mean or a target if that is your reference).
Edit `posLabel` and `negLabel` to say what above and below mean.
Keep the rail: the reference value and the share of people in below-reference units.
For a Japanese page keep word-break:keep-all and break the headline at a phrase boundary.

resources.title: Slope chart: paired values at two occasions
resources.purpose: Track the same entities between two occasions on one shared scale so changes in level and in rank read together, without implying the years in between.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Track the same entities between two occasions so changes in level and in rank read together.
Modify: Replace `lines` (a = first occasion, b = second) and `occasions`. The highlighted line is the largest fall; switch the sort to the largest rise if that is the story. Labels spread themselves to avoid collisions.
Invariant: One vertical scale for both occasions; straight lines only between the two measured points; say that intervening years are not shown.
Static: Already static. For a build, pass build:{by:"mark"} to draw lines one at a time, the highlighted one last.
deriveSteps: Replace `lines` (a = first occasion, b = second) and the two `occasions` labels.
Choose the story line: the largest fall is selected by default; flip the sort for the largest rise.
Keep one domain for both axes; it is computed from all values.
State in the source line that only the two occasions are measured.

resources.title: Paired intervals
resources.purpose: Show the distance between two measurements
resources.notes:
Purpose: Show before and after for each category on one shared scale, so the level and the change read together.
Modify: Replace `queues`; the headline count, the rail numbers and the change column recompute. Rename aLabel/bLabel to your two moments or conditions.
Invariant: Both ends share one axis and unit; rows sort by change; the change column states its sign; a rise is reported, not hidden among falls.
Static: Already static. For a build, pass build:{by:"mark"} to reveal one row per click.
deriveSteps: Identify quantities, denominator, uncertainty definition and units.
Replace schematic geometry with one data-to-pixel mapping.
Recompute ticks, direct labels, reference marks and extremes.
Check missing/negative values and compare source totals.

resources.title: Bullet chart: actual against a named target
resources.purpose: Compare each measure with its own named target and qualitative ranges, side by side even when units differ, with attainment printed.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Compare each measure with its own named target (plan) and say how far off it is, measures with different units side by side.
Modify: Replace `kpis` (value, plan, the three range edges, unit format). The attainment column, the accented worst measure and the headline recompute.
Invariant: Every bar starts at zero on its own row scale; the plan tick is labelled in the key; attainment is printed, so no one has to judge lengths across rows with different units.
Static: Already static. For a build, grow the actual bars after the bands and ticks are shown.
deriveSteps: Replace `kpis`: value, plan, the three range edges (poor / satisfactory / good) and a number format per measure.
Rename `quality` if your bands mean something else (for example risk levels).
The worst attainment takes the accent and drives the headline; check the measure name reads well in a sentence.
Keep 3–7 rows; more measures belong on a second page.

resources.title: Dot plot: position-only comparison on a non-zero axis
resources.purpose: Compare quantities by position alone, so the axis can start near the data and small but real differences between groups stay visible.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Compare quantities by position alone, without filled bars, so the axis can start near the data and small but real differences stay visible.
Modify: Replace `wards` and `series`. Rows sort by the first series; the range annotation, its end values and the headline recompute.
Invariant: Dots, not bars, whenever the axis does not start at zero; the axis start is stated in the description; every row uses the same scale and series order.
Static: Already static. For a build, show one series first, then the other.
deriveSteps: Replace `wards` and `series`; rows sort by the first series, which takes the accent colour.
Keep the computed domain (it starts near the data) and say in the description where the axis starts.
The range annotation spans the first series' minimum and maximum; point it at the series your headline is about.
Use bars instead if zero is meaningful and the axis must start there.

resources.title: Waffle: a share as countable squares
resources.purpose: Show a share as 100 countable squares that each stand for the same stated amount, with the absolute volume beside it.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Show a share as countable squares, so "23 in 100" can be checked by counting, with the absolute volume beside it.
Modify: Replace `flows` (first item is the share the page is about). Counts are rounded once and the largest part absorbs the remainder; the key, the volume block and the headline recompute.
Invariant: 100 squares, each worth the same stated amount; key counts equal the squares drawn; the rounding rule is visible in the code, not hidden in the drawing.
Static: Already static. For a build, fill the highlighted squares first.
deriveSteps: Replace `flows` with your parts in one unit; the first item is the share the page is about and takes the accent.
Counts are rounded once with the largest part absorbing the remainder, so the key always matches the squares.
Rewrite the left block as the absolute quantity behind the share, and the footnote as the value of one square.
Use a second waffle, not a bigger grid, to compare two wholes.

resources.title: Lollipop: magnitudes with less ink
resources.purpose: Compare many magnitudes from a shared zero with thin stems and end dots, so endpoints and a decision threshold carry the reading instead of heavy bars.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Compare many magnitudes from a shared zero with a thin stem and an end dot, so the endpoints and a threshold carry the reading instead of heavy bars.
Modify: Replace `sites` and `needed`. Rows sort themselves; the qualifying sites take the accent, and the threshold line, its gaps around labels and the headline recompute.
Invariant: Stems start at zero and share one scale; the threshold is drawn and named, not implied; the accent marks only the sites that meet it.
Static: Already static. For a build, reveal the threshold first, then the stems.
deriveSteps: Replace `sites` and `needed`; rows sort themselves and every item meeting the threshold takes the accent.
Define the measure precisely in the dek (what counts as a usable unit).
Keep the threshold line: it breaks automatically where a value label sits on it.
Use plain bars when there are fewer than about six rows.

resources.title: Waterfall: an additive bridge between two totals
resources.purpose: Explain how signed contributions move one total to another, with the closing total computed from the bridge so it always adds up.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Explain how signed contributions move one total to another, in the order a finance reader expects.
Modify: Replace `opening` and `drivers`. Leave the closing total without a value: the chart computes the running sum (and refuses a typed total that does not add up). The headline sums and the annotated driver recompute.
Invariant: Every floating bar starts where the previous one ended; totals start at zero; signs are printed; the closing total equals the opening total plus the labelled contributions.
Static: Already static. For a build, pass build:{by:"mark"} to add one driver per click.
tags: ウォーターフォールチャート
deriveSteps: Replace `opening` and `drivers`; leave the closing total without a value so the chart computes it.
Order drivers the way your finance team reads them (commercial first, then costs, then currency).
Group the drivers the headline sums in `growthDrivers`; the largest reduction is found automatically.
Attach at most one annotation, to the driver the audience will ask about.

resources.title: Registered before and after: one geometry, two states
resources.purpose: Compare the same geometry in two states drawn on one scale with fixed edges aligned, so only what changed can look different and the change is stated.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Compare the same geometry in two states (here a street cross-section) with camera, scale and fixed edges identical, so the eye sees only what changed.
Modify: Replace `states` (each space: use, width in metres, people per hour). Segments, lane lines, totals, the ratio and the kerb check recompute; the module throws if the two states do not span the same width.
Invariant: One metre scale for both states (scale bar shown); building lines and kerbs registered and carried across with guides; changed spaces take the accent family, unchanged ones stay grey; the change is stated, not just drawn.
Static: Already static. As motion, keep the strip and let the segments morph between states.
deriveSteps: Replace `states`: each space with its use, width in metres and the measured quantity; both states must span the same width or the module throws.
Map uses to fills in `style`: changed spaces take the accent family, unchanged ones stay grey.
Keep the registration guides (building lines, kerbs) and the scale bar; they prove the comparison is like for like.
Rewrite the dek to name what changed and what did not.

resources.title: Indexed lines: relative change from a common start
resources.purpose: Compare relative change from one common starting point when series differ greatly in size, while keeping their absolute size on the page.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Compare relative change from one common starting point when the series differ greatly in size, and keep their absolute size in view.
Modify: Replace `years` and `capacity`; rebase() indexes each series to its first value. The fastest grower takes the accent; the rail and headline recompute absolute additions.
Invariant: The base year and base value (=100) are printed on the axis and the reference line; an index never stands in for size, so absolute values appear beside it.
Static: Already static. For a build, draw the 100 line first, then the series.
deriveSteps: Replace `years` and `capacity`; rebase() indexes each series to its first value.
State the base year in the unit label and the reference line.
The fastest-growing series takes the accent; the rail shows absolute change for it and for the largest contributor.
If any series starts near zero, show absolute values instead: an index from a tiny base exaggerates.

resources.title: Small multiples: one shape per panel on shared axes
resources.purpose: Compare the shape and height of several series by repeating one small chart with identical axes and the same reference line in every panel.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Compare the shape and height of many series by repeating one small chart with identical axes, instead of overlaying them or switching scales.
Modify: Replace `days` (one array per panel, aligned to `hours`). The shared y-range, the all-days average, every peak label and the headline recompute; the spare grid cell holds the key.
Invariant: Every panel uses the same y and x scales (stated in the key); the reference line is the same average in every panel; only the panel the headline names takes the accent.
Static: Already static. For a build, reveal panels in reading order.
deriveSteps: Replace `days` (one array per panel aligned to `hours`) and the panel names.
Keep the shared y-range computed from all panels and the all-panel average drawn behind each line.
The panel with the highest peak takes the accent; change the selection if your story is another panel.
Keep a spare grid cell for the key, or drop the key if the panels are self-explanatory.

resources.title: Unit array: an absolute count you can inspect
resources.purpose: Make an absolute count inspectable by drawing one mark per person or event, grouped so each group can be counted and compared.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Make an absolute count inspectable: one mark per person (or event), grouped so each group can be counted and compared.
Modify: Replace `deaths` and the context numbers. Rows widen to the largest group so lengths compare like bars; the total, the accented group and the headline recompute.
Invariant: One mark always means one unit, stated on the page; counts are printed beside each group and add up to the total; no mark is scaled or merged.
Static: Already static. For a build, reveal groups one at a time, the accented group last.
deriveSteps: Replace `deaths` with your groups and counts, and the `as` phrase each group needs in the headline.
Rows widen to the largest group, so the rows also compare like bars; keep counts under about 60 per group.
Keep the key that says what one mark is.
Use the rail for the total and one context fact taken from the same records.

resources.title: Quadrant: alternatives on two stated dimensions
resources.purpose: Place alternatives on two stated dimensions and name what each quadrant implies, while showing on the page that the positions are judgments.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Locate alternatives on two stated dimensions and name what each quadrant implies, while making clear that positions are judgments.
Modify: Replace `apps` (panel scores 1–5), `mid` and `quadrants`. Dots, quadrant membership, the accented quadrant, the panel note and the headline recompute; quadrant names stay in the bands no score can reach.
Invariant: Both axes are titled with their good direction and their scale; who judged, and how, is stated on the page; items are never nudged across a line for neatness, only their labels move.
Static: Already static. For a build, show the quadrants first, then the items.
deriveSteps: Replace `apps` with your items scored 1–5 on both axes, and `mid` with your threshold.
Rename `quadrants` to the actions they imply; quadrant names stay in the bands no score can reach.
Say who scored and how in the dek and source line.
Never nudge a dot across a line; only labels move to avoid collisions.

resources.title: Histogram: a binned distribution with a disclosed bin width
resources.purpose: Shows how a measured quantity is distributed so a pile-up at a target, a long tail or a gap is visible instead of being averaged away.
