resources.purpose: A common reference moves with the quantities it defines.
resources.notes:
Purpose: When values are re-expressed against a new reference (a new normal, a new datum), move the values and the old reference together as one coordinate system, so every distance between them is visibly preserved.
Modify: Replace `summer` (anomalies against the old reference) and `newPeriod`; the shift is the mean over the new period, and the translation, the new zero and both measurements recompute.
Invariant: One translation, computed from the data, moves the series and the old zero line as a unit; the axis and its tick labels never change; the new zero is drawn in place and named; the latest value is measured against both references.
Static: The final build shows the shifted series, the old zero (named) inside it, the new zero, and both measurements of the latest year.

resources.title: Return a detail to its larger context
resources.purpose: A close reading becomes one part of a wider explanation.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Start from a close reading (one week, every value labelled), then zoom the same bars out until that week is one part of the season, and name the pattern it belongs to.
Modify: Replace `maxTemp` and `transports` (one value per day from `start`); set `week` to the close reading and `hotAt` to the threshold. The zoom factor, labels and shares recompute.
Invariant: The zoom scales the time axis only, so bar heights (the values) never change; the same bars move, nothing is redrawn; the week stays outlined after the zoom.
Static: The final build shows the whole summer, the outlined week and the 5 days at or above 37℃ in the accent.

resources.title: Show the condition that enables a transfer
resources.purpose: Shows every enabling condition being met and the gate changing state before the downstream transfer happens, with timing on its own axis.
resources.notes:
Purpose: The gate changes before the downstream result appears: every release condition is met first, then the lot moves.
Modify: Edit `checks` (name, spec, result, start/end day, pass). The gate opens only when every check passes; set one `pass` to false and the gate stays shut and the lot stays in quarantine.
Invariant: Conditions are visible (as pending outlines) from the first build; the gate state changes in its own build; the transfer happens after it, and the lot is one element that moves through the gate.
Static: The final build shows completed checks, the open gate and the lot in released stock. A state change is not proof of physical timing; the day axis carries the timing.
deriveSteps: Edit `checks` (name, spec, result, start and end day, pass); the gate opens only if every check passes.
Set `lot` (identifier, product, start date); the release date and day count recompute.
Set one `pass` to false to show a gate that stays shut and a lot that stays put.
Keep the state change of the gate and the transfer in separate builds.

resources.title: Change emphasis, not the underlying result
resources.purpose: The comparison remains available while attention changes.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Walk attention through a comparison in two stages (first the baseline, then the alternative) while both results stay on the chart the whole time, and end with both at full strength.
Modify: Replace `profiles` (24 hourly values each); peaks, the shift in hours and the percentage recompute. Keep the line that the headline names in the accent.
Invariant: Data, scales and line geometry are identical in every build; only opacity changes (never below about a fifth, so the other series stays readable); each peak note dims and returns with its own line.
Static: The final build shows both profiles at full strength with both peaks and the shift between them.

resources.title: Unstack labels onto a readable rail
resources.purpose: Labels are given space without changing the named objects.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Give labels room without changing what they name: the legend labels travel to a rail beside the line ends, spaced so none collide, and leaders tie each to its line.
Modify: Replace `groups` (one index series each); rail slots come from spreadLabels on the end values, so they adapt when ends bunch or spread. Keep at most four or five series in categorical colors.
Invariant: Lines, scales and colors never change; each label keeps its color and moves as one element (translate only) from its legend slot to its rail slot; leaders appear after the labels arrive.
Static: The final build shows direct labels on the rail with end values, and the peak annotated (the legend swatches are gone).

resources.title: Reorder rows while preserving row identity
resources.purpose: Rows move through separate horizontal lanes to avoid label collisions.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Re-sort a table by another column so the audience can follow every row to its new place and see the pattern the new order reveals.
Modify: Replace `hospitals`; the sort, each row’s lane (centre and angle), the k-fastest/k-lowest test and the headline recompute. Sort ties keep the previous order.
Invariant: Each row is one opaque group that moves as a unit and stays upright; rows moving up travel on the left lane in front, rows moving down on the right lane behind, so names never interleave; columns and scales do not change.
Static: The final build shows the sorted table, the highlighted mortality bars and the bracket. Export build 0 as a page if the alphabetical order is itself needed.

resources.title: Expand a boundary without moving the evidence
resources.purpose: The observed object stays put when the discussed scope becomes wider.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Widen the scope under discussion (one month, its season, several seasons) without moving or rescaling the evidence, so the audience sees the same bars judged against a larger context.
Modify: Replace `outbreaks` and `first`; winters, the peak, the boundary transforms, the statements and the headline recompute. Define seasons to match your domain.
Invariant: Bars and axes never move; one boundary element widens by transforms computed from the data; each statement is computed only from the bars inside its boundary; the observed bar keeps the accent throughout.
Static: The final build shows the widest boundary, every winter total and the comparison with last winter.

resources.title: Pull apart independent factors
resources.purpose: The representation separates factors without implying a measured contribution.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Separate a quantity into the independent factors it is the product of, shown side by side on one scale, without implying that each factor contributed a measurable share.
Modify: Replace `raw` (one series per factor) and the identity in `revenue`; indices, the panel transform, labels and the headline recompute.
Invariant: The revenue panel moves and narrows as one coordinate system (one computed transform) while its labels travel at full size; all panels share one index scale; factors sit next to each other, never stacked; the page says the changes multiply.
Static: The final build shows the four panels, the operators and each factor’s change in its own units.

resources.title: Let the evidence answer the question
resources.purpose: A question remains readable when supporting evidence enters.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Pose the question in the headline and keep it fixed while the evidence enters underneath; state the answer only after the evidence is on screen.
Modify: Replace `teams` (group, before, during); the group means, percentage changes, the count of teams that improved and the answer recompute.
Invariant: The question never moves or changes; build 0 names what will be compared and on which scale; every team is drawn before the means; the answer quotes numbers computed from the drawn data and names the comparison group.
Static: The final build shows all teams, both means, the highlighted pilot mean and the answer.

resources.title: Move the window instead of stretching the subject
resources.purpose: The same source is revealed through a shifting crop.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Show how one photograph serves several formats by moving and reshaping the crop window over a fixed image, never by scaling or stretching the subject.
Modify: Replace the photo, `subject` (its box in source pixels) and `formats` (crop boxes in source pixels); the share of the frame kept and the whole-subject check recompute.
Invariant: The image is drawn once at one scale; only the window, its veil and its label move (one computed matrix per format). Outside the window the photo is veiled, not hidden.
Static: The final build shows the 9:16 window on the photo and all three formats listed.

resources.title: Reveal the thought in readable phrases
resources.purpose: Reveal semantic phrases, not individual letters.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Let the audience read a quotation phrase by phrase, at the pace it is spoken, instead of meeting a block of text or a letter-by-letter typewriter.
Modify: Split `phrases` where a speaker pauses (Japanese: at 文節 boundaries; English: at clause or prepositional-phrase boundaries). Replace `answers` with the survey result that says how common the quoted experience is.
Invariant: Each build adds one whole phrase in reading order; earlier phrases never move; the attribution arrives with the last phrase; the survey bar for the quoted behaviour is the only accent.
Static: The final build shows the full quotation, its attribution and the survey bars.

resources.title: Change the two values on the same scale
resources.purpose: Two changing bars retain a common baseline and units.
resources.notes:
Purpose: Change two related values together on one shared baseline and unit, so their difference is read as a distance that is re-measured at every step.
Modify: Replace `years` and the two `areas` (one value per year); column scales, counted labels, ghost ticks, the gap bracket and the rail recompute.
Invariant: Both columns rescale from the same zero with transforms computed from the data; labels count from the previous value; earlier values stay as labelled ticks; the gap is always urban minus rural on the same axis.
Static: The final build shows the latest values, both earlier ticks per column and the gap history in the rail.

resources.title: Give the evidence the larger region
resources.purpose: Give the evidence the larger region
resources.notes:
Purpose: Use when one exhibit carries the argument and the words only point at it: a result with uncertainty, a trend, a ranking. The evidence is the optical primary; the headline states what it shows; the rail adds only what the chart cannot say (one summary number and the limit of the claim).
Modify: Replace `corridors` (estimate, interval, the explanatory variable) and `minLane`; the sort, the break between groups, the headline range, the rail number and the named exceptions recompute. Keep the rail to one number and one or two sentences; if it needs more, the claim is not ready.
Invariant: 3 : 1 split of the 1152 px measure (828 px evidence, 48 px gap, 276 px rail); the figure is drawn at its region size so labels are true 16–18 px; intervals stay on the same row as their estimates; rows that do not support the claim are shown in context grey, not removed.
Static: Already static. For a talk, a build can reveal the short-lane rows after the claim, but the final state must show all rows.

resources.title: Keep number, unit and scope together
resources.purpose: Keep number, unit and scope together
resources.notes:
Purpose: Use when one quantity is the message and it is easily misread: a ratio, a rate, a per-unit figure, anything with a denominator or a measurement boundary. The number, its unit and its scope are one block; the proof below shows where the figure sits among its observations and beside the number people will compare it with.
Modify: Replace `homes` with measured values and `rated` with the figure it gets confused with; the hero number, the quartiles, the dots and the count recompute. Rewrite the unit and the scope line for your quantity (what was measured, where, over what period, what is included).
Invariant: The unit sits on the number's baseline and the scope directly under it — never in a footnote or a different column; the comparison number carries its own scope; the hero figure is ink, its mark in the proof is the one accent.
Static: Already static.

resources.title: Align three small views without adding cards
resources.purpose: Align three small views without adding cards
resources.notes:
Purpose: Use when one dataset must answer two or three different questions (who changed, by how much, who is missing) and each needs its own view. Alignment makes them one exhibit: the reader compares across panels instead of reading three slides.
Modify: Replace `pupils` (two measurements per unit, null when missing, and a reason); the counts, median, dots and grid recompute. Rewrite each question as a plain question and each answer as the computed result. Keep three panels or fewer; a fourth question is a new page.
Invariant: Equal 4-column panels (368 px, 24 px gutters) sharing four lines: question, answer, plot top, baseline. Whitespace separates the panels, not boxes or tinted fields. The same units appear in every view (one mark = one pupil); the one accent is the median the headline names; missing observations stay visible as hollow marks.
Static: Already static.

resources.title: Put the qualification where it applies
resources.purpose: Put the qualification where it applies
resources.notes:
Purpose: Use when most of the evidence supports the claim but one or two items are not comparable (a relocation, a closure, a definition change). The reason is set in a rail at the height of the item it explains, so the qualification is read in the same glance as the odd number — not in a footnote the room never reaches.
Modify: Replace `stores`; mark non-comparable rows with `why` and the facts that explain them, and write `noteFor` for your reasons. Sort order, bars, the reference total, the notes' positions and leaders recompute.
Invariant: A note's first line shares its row's centre line; the leader runs at that height; non-comparable rows stay in the chart in context grey (never deleted) and are excluded from the headline total; the accent marks only the comparable actuals the headline counts.
Static: Already static.

resources.title: Write the question in natural Japanese
resources.purpose: Write the question in natural Japanese
resources.notes:
Purpose: Use when a Japanese audience came to the meeting with a question (should we extend the hours? did the change work?). The headline asks it the way they would say it, the answer sits beside it in one sentence that leads with the verdict, and the chart below carries the one caveat at the place it applies.
Modify: Replace `hours` and the closing times; the totals, the gain, the new-hours sum and the dip recompute. Write the question in plain spoken Japanese (〜のか / 〜だろうか), break it only at a phrase boundary, and start the answer with the verdict (増えた。/ 変わらなかった。).
Invariant: No English labels or eyebrows; numbers in Latin tabular figures with the unit attached (2,412人, 18時台); full-width punctuation; the headline breaks after 、 never inside a phrase; the accent is the current-year series and its one annotation; the caveat is written as a sentence where the eye lands.
Static: Already static.

resources.title: Let structure and scope share the page
resources.purpose: Let structure and scope share the page
resources.notes:
Purpose: Use when a result depends on a mechanism and the audience will generalise it: a fix, a treatment, a process change. The left two thirds explain how it works; the right third shows the conditions under which it has actually been shown, with the real workload plotted against them, so the limit is read with the mechanism and not discovered later.
Modify: Replace `expiry` with your own timing (who acts, who waits, how long) and `tested`/`keys` with your test envelope and the population you will apply it to. The diagram rows, the fan-out, the envelope and the count of keys outside it recompute.
Invariant: Mechanism and scope are side by side at the same top line, never mechanism on one slide and caveats on another; the scope is drawn (an envelope with the real cases in it), not only stated; the one accent is the single action the mechanism turns on; the headline names the limit in its quiet clause.
Static: Already static. As a build, reveal the scope panel after the mechanism, never instead of it.

resources.title: Build a continuous explanatory path
resources.purpose: Build a continuous explanatory path
resources.notes:
Purpose: Use for any process where a quantity is transformed step by step (a harvest to a product, applicants to hires, raw rows to a reported figure). The reader follows one continuous band instead of jumping between boxes; each state names what it hands on, each loss is named where it leaves, and every number can be traced back to the start.
Modify: Replace `start` and `steps` (state handed on, loss, what the loss is); the masses, band thickness, peel-offs and labels recompute, and the totals always reconcile. Keep five to seven steps; more becomes a table. Swap the photograph for the real end product or drop it.
Invariant: Thickness is proportional to quantity on one scale; the band never breaks or changes scale; losses leave on the same side and are labelled where they land; the state label sits at the start of its segment so each number reads as handed on to the next.
Static: Already static. A build can grow the band left to right, one step per click.
